description: Evaluation questions for stage 6. Evidence quotes are verified against data/processed_chunks.json by build_evaluation_questions.py.

questions.question: What were the last words of Helen Stoner's sister?
questions.expected_answer: "It was the band! The speckled band!"
evidence: she suddenly shrieked out in a voice which I shall never forget, 'Oh, my God! Helen! It was the band! The speckled band!'
a fresh convulsion seized her and choked her words
questions.support_note: Helen narrates her sister's dying cry; a convulsion then stopped her from saying more.

questions.question: Where did the ventilator in Helen Stoner's room lead?
questions.expected_answer: Into another room (Dr. Roylott's), not to the outside air.
evidence: open a ventilator into another room
her sister could smell Dr. Roylott's cigar. Now, of course that suggested at once that there must be a communication between the two rooms
questions.support_note: 035: it opens into another room, not outside. 041: that room is Dr. Roylott's.

questions.question: What did Holmes find on top of the iron safe in Dr. Roylott's room?
evidence: a small saucer of milk which stood on the top of it
questions.support_note: Same passage: the iron safe in Roylott's room and the saucer of milk on top of it.

questions.question: Why could Helen Stoner not move her bed?
questions.expected_answer: It was clamped to the floor.
evidence: It was clamped to the floor
The lady could not move her bed
questions.support_note: Holmes states both the cause and the consequence.

questions.question: What animls did Dr. Roylot keep at Stoke Moran?
questions.original_question: What animals did Dr. Roylott keep at Stoke Moran?
questions.expected_answer: A cheetah and a baboon (he had a passion for Indian animals).
evidence: He has a passion also for Indian animals
he has at this moment a cheetah and a baboon, which wander freely over his grounds
questions.support_note: Helen describes her stepfather's animals on the family estate (Stoke Moran).

questions.question: What was the speckld band realy?
questions.original_question: What was the speckled band really?
questions.expected_answer: A swamp adder, the deadliest snake in India.
questions.support_note: Holmes identifies the 'speckled band' on Roylott's head.

questions.question: What colour were the curtains in Helen Stoner's bedroom?
questions.note: The story never describes curtains in the bedroom.

questions.question: Who picked up the hat and the goose after the fight on Tottenham Court Road?
evidence: he was left in possession of the field of battle, and also of the spoils of victory in the shape of this battered hat and a most unimpeachable Christmas goose
questions.support_note: 003 names Peterson the commissionaire and says he found the hat; 004 says the fight left him with the hat and the goose. The previous quotes only said he walked down Tottenham Court Road.

questions.question: What initials were written inside the hat?
questions.expected_answer: H. B. (the card on the goose read 'For Mrs. Henry Baker').
evidence: the initials "H. B." were scrawled upon one side
Henry Baker' was printed upon a small card which was tied to the bird's left leg, and it is also true that the initials 'H. B.' are legible upon the lining of this hat
questions.support_note: 006 gives the initials; the link to Henry Baker comes from the card quoted in 005, not from the hat itself.

questions.question: Where did Peterson's wife find the blue stone?
questions.expected_answer: In the crop of the goose.
evidence: See what my wife found in its crop!
questions.support_note: Peterson, holding the blue stone, says his wife found it in the goose's crop.

questions.question: Who was accused of stealing the Countess of Morcar's jewel?
evidence: John Horner, 26, plumber, was brought up upon the charge of having upon the 22nd inst., abstracted from the jewel-case of the Countess of Morcar
questions.support_note: The newspaper report states the charge against Horner.

questions.question: Wich dealer in Covent Gardn sold the geese to the Alpha Inn?
questions.original_question: Which dealer in Covent Garden sold the geese to the Alpha Inn?
evidence: I got the two dozen from a salesman in Covent Garden
questions.support_note: The landlord of the Alpha names the Covent Garden salesman.

questions.question: What was the real name of the man who called himself John Robinsn?
questions.original_question: What was the real name of the man who called himself John Robinson?
evidence: my real name is James Ryder
questions.support_note: The stranger first gives the alias, then his real name.

questions.question: What colour was the Countess of Morcar's carriage?
questions.note: No carriage is mentioned in the story.

questions.question: How much was Jabez Wilson paid each week by the Red-Headed League?
questions.support_note: The advertisement and Duncan Ross both state the pay.

questions.question: Who was caught in the bank cellar at the end of the case?
questions.support_note: Said by Holmes to the man coming up through the hole in the bank cellar floor.

questions.question: Why was Jabez Wilson paid to copy the Encyclopaedia?
questions.expected_answer: To get him out of the way for a number of hours every day.
evidence: to get this not over-bright pawnbroker out of the way for a number of hours every day
questions.support_note: Holmes's explanation: the League and the copying only existed to keep the pawnbroker away.
questions.note: Same question as the Watson diagnostic; the evidence uses different words.

questions.question: Why did Holmes beat the pavment with his stik?
questions.original_question: Why did Holmes beat the pavement with his stick?
questions.expected_answer: To find out whether the cellar stretched out in front or behind.
evidence: I surprised you by beating upon the pavement with my stick. I was ascertaining whether the cellar stretched out in front or behind.
questions.support_note: Holmes explains it himself; 'the shop' was removed from the expected answer because the quote does not say it.

questions.question: What was stored in the crates in the bank cellar?
questions.expected_answer: French gold: napoleons, 2,000 in each crate, packed between layers of lead foil.
evidence: borrowed for that purpose 30,000 napoleons from the Bank of France
The crate upon which I sit contains 2,000 napoleons packed between layers of lead foil
questions.support_note: Merryweather confirms it is the French gold and describes one crate.

questions.question: What was the name of the girl who cooked for Jabez Wilson?
questions.note: The girl is mentioned only as 'a girl of fourteen' (red_headed_league_010); her name is never given.
